review_notes: Read all 134 lines of the target file, including the basis construction, its representation lemmas, the base-change linear-map lemma, the freeness instance, and toMatrix_baseChange. Also inspected the relevant supporting declarations: Basis.linearMap_apply_apply and Module.Basis.end in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/ToLin.lean, baseChange_tmul in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Tower.lean, TensorProduct.inductionOn, TensorProduct.smul_tmul', TensorProduct.tmul_ite and TensorProduct.tmul_zero in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Defs.lean, and Module.Basis.baseChange in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basis.lean. The only well-supported simplification I found is in the final step of Module.Basis.baseChange_linearMap: the if-case split can be replaced by an explicit use of TensorProduct.tmul_ite. I did not execute Lean, so the proposed replacement is not verified by compilation; it is a concrete proposed tactic block, not a claimed compiled proof. Other proofs are already short, and alternatives I considered (e.g. rewriting basis_repr_symm_apply' through basis_apply) were mostly stylistic or longer rather than clearer.

findings.problem: The final step uses `split <;> simp only [TensorProduct.tmul_zero]`, which performs an if-case split merely to commute the tensor product with the `if` that remains after the linearMap rewrites. This hides the key distributivity fact and adds a case split that a reader has to follow unnecessarily.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the final line with an explicit rewrite using the named lemma `TensorProduct.tmul_ite`, which states exactly that a tensor product distributes over an if-expression:

```lean
  simp only [TensorProduct.tmul_ite, TensorProduct.tmul_zero]
```

So the end of the proof becomes:

```lean
  conv_lhs => simp only [basis_apply, baseChange_tmul]
  simp_rw [Basis.linearMap_apply_apply, basis_apply]
  simp only [TensorProduct.tmul_ite, TensorProduct.tmul_zero]
```
findings.benefit: The reader sees the mathematical reason directly: `1 ⊗ₜ (if h then b i else 0)` becomes `if h then 1 ⊗ₜ b i else 0` by `TensorProduct.tmul_ite`, with `tmul_zero` handling the zero branch. This removes an unnecessary case split and uses a well-named lemma instead of forcing the reader to inspect both branches of `split`.

evidence.excerpt:
theorem tmul_ite (x₁ : M) (x₂ : N) (P : Prop) [Decidable P] :
    (x₁ ⊗ₜ[R] if P then x₂ else 0) = if P then x₁ ⊗ₜ x₂ else 0 := by split_ifs <;> simp
